title: Teams retires off-network invitations that onboard external people to Teams Free; federation with Teams Free stays
summary: MC1546409 says Microsoft Teams will retire the flow that lets work or school users invite someone who cannot be found in Teams to create a Teams Free account and join a chat, both by email invitation and by sharing a link to chat. Rollout starts in early December 2026 and should complete by late December. Chat with existing Teams Free users remains available, subject to your external-access policies, and team, channel and meeting collaboration does not change.
why: A user-driven path that pulled unmanaged consumer accounts into business chats disappears, which narrows an external-collaboration channel you could not govern well. Expect helpdesk tickets from users who relied on it; the supported alternatives are guest access or the external person creating a Teams Free account independently.
todo: Update user and helpdesk guidance before 6 December 2026, as Microsoft recommends.
Review the Teams external access setting for chat with unmanaged Teams accounts and decide whether chat with Teams Free users should be allowed at all.
Point recurring external collaboration to B2B guest access, where Conditional Access and access reviews apply.
effective_note: Rolling out early to late December 2026, worldwide (MC1546409).
